slides.title: Shelves that stack
slides.text: The Counting House stores its stock on shelves. Joining two shelf counts is addition: stack them in columns, place over place, and add each stack.

slides.title: Trading up
slides.text: Ten loose ones fill one box, so they trade up for one ten. That trade is regrouping. Nothing is lost. The value just moves house.

visual.label: Trading up: 8 ones and 5 ones make 13 ones, which trade for 1 ten and 3 ones

rows.label: After the trade: the same 13, packed

focus.cue: 8 ones and 5 ones join on the shelf: 13 ones.
Ten of them trade up for 1 ten. 3 ones stay loose.

slides.title: Rough first, then join
slides.text: Rough first: 268 + 475 is about 300 + 500 = 800, a bit less. Now join them with trades.

slides.title: Stretch: Four-digit joins
slides.text: The same trades work one place higher. In 3,486 + 2,757, trade at the ones, the tens and the hundreds. The answer is 6,243.

words.means: joining two or more amounts into one total
to trade ten of one place for one of the next place
a vertical stack of digits in the same place

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Sum Racer. It opens on the Addition to 100 track, adding questions only, and it stays there. Win the race: when a column passes ten, say the trade out loud.
